question: Designing an 'Agent Decision Record' (AgDR) system — a new record type for judgment calls Claude makes autonomously during delegated work, reviewed by the human after the fact. What prior philosophies govern decision-record systems, delegation guardrails, review-after-the-fact workflows, and keeping conventions wired into consumers?
answer: Four prior philosophies bear directly on AgDR design: (1) Decision records must be wired to consumers, not just written — each AgDR must link to the task/delegation context that produced it or it becomes an orphaned audit artifact. (2) Review-after-the-fact is structurally weaker than upfront gates — PHI-012 holds cross-phase decision pollution is real; AgDR inverts decide-then-review deliberately and should declare under what conditions the human can unwind vs only acknowledge. (3) Escalation beats silent fixes — PHI-026's three-option structure (inline-fix, accept-as-deferred-risk, kick to separate work) maps cleanly to AgDR review states. (4) Dual-defense over-design is a risk — static/convention enforcement over runtime gates when failure mode is authoring error. Gap: the bank has no PHI on which judgment-call categories are delegable without prior approval vs always-escalate — the AgDR spec must define that boundary from scratch.
